chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Qāsim, from ʿAlī, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about the ghusl of the two ʿIds: Is it obligatory? He said, “It is a sunnah.” I said: Then [what about] Friday? He said, “It is a sunnah.”

So this report indicates that what the hadith of ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā from Samāʿah contains regarding the mention of the obligation of the ghusl of the two ʿIds, what is intended by it is what we have mentioned concerning the emphasis of the sunnah.

key_terms.الْجُمُعَةُ: Friday, referring here to the Friday ghusl
key_terms.الْخَبَرُ: the report or hadith being cited as evidence
key_terms.تَأْكِيدِ السُّنَّةِ: the strong emphasis and confirmation of a recommended practice
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: an established recommended practice, not obligatory here
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْعِيدَيْنِ: the ritual bath associated with the two ʿId festivals
key_terms.وُجُوبِ: the expression of obligatoriness mentioned in another report

ai.seo_question: Is the ghusl of the two ʿIds and Friday obligatory or only sunnah in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report states that the ghusl for the two ʿIds and for Friday is sunnah, not obligatory. It also clarifies that reports expressing its 'obligation' are to be understood as emphasizing the strength and confirmation of the sunnah rather than legal obligation.
